questions.question: 'Paika' is a folk dance performed by members of the society in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paika:**

 
 
• Paika is a **Sadani Nagpuri martial folk dance** from the Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh (Chhota Nagpur plateaus region).
 
• It also known as** Painki and Paiki**.
 
• Participants in the dance **wear dhotis**, which are **turbans adorned with peacock feathers.**
 
• They dance to the **sounds of Nagara, Dhak, Shehnai, and Narsingh** musical instruments while **holding a sword in their right hand** and a **shield in their left**.
 
• **Paik served as foot soilders** throughout the **medieval period**. It displays bravery and is carried out by guys.
 
• It is done at events like weddings. 
 
• The main performers are **Rautia, who were soldiers in Chotanagpur during the Nagvanshi dynasty**. In the districts of Khunti and Mayurbhanj, some **Munda tribe** members also perform it.

• Santhali

questions.question: Which one of them is NOT a fundamental duty?

options.text: Cherishing the ideas of national freedom struggle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Duty to cast your vote.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fundamental Duties:

 
 
• Part IV A of the Indian Constitution contains Article 51A, which deals with the Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Soviet Constitution (USSR) is where the idea of fundamental duties originated.
 
• Fundamental Duties were recommended in 1976 by the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Ten Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
 
• Fundamental duties are not subject to legal action unless specifically stated in a provision, in contrast to fundamental rights, which are justiciable.
 
 
 
• Right to vote:
 
 
• **Article 326** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to vote. According to this article, "every State's Legislative Assembly and House of People elections shall be conducted on the **basis of adult suffrage**, meaning that any **Indian citizen** who is **not less than eighteen years **old may participate."
 
• It is **not a part of Fundamental duty **but it is a **legal right** and a moral responsibility of every citizen to vote in the elections.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added ten fundamental duties.
 
• The 86th Amendment to the Constitution was passed in 2002, adding the eleventh fundamental duty.
 
• The list of Fundamental Duties as mentioned in the Article 51A:

 
 

 
 
S.No.

 
 
 
Fundamental Duties

 
 
 

 
 
1.

 
 
 
Abide by the Indian Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem

 
 
 

 
 
2.

 
 
 
Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom

 
 
 

 
 
3.

 
 
 
Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

 
 
 

 
 
4.

 
 
 
Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so

 
 
 

 
 
5.

 
 
 
Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women

 
 
 

 
 
6.

 
 
 
Value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture

 
 
 

 
 
7.

 
 
 
Protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife and to have compassion for living creatures

 
 
 

 
 
8.

 
 
 
Develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform

 
 
 

 
 
9.

 
 
 
Safeguard public property and to abjure violence

 
 
 

 
 
10.

 
 
 
Strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement

 
 
 

 
 
11.

 
 
 
Provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

questions.question: Ziyauddin Barani wrote his chronicle‘s first version in ______ year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1356.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ziyauddin Barani composed his first chronicle in 1356 **and a second one two years later.
 
• **Ziyauddin Barani:**
 
 
• Ziauddin Barani **(1285–1358)** was a Indian Muslim **political thinker, historian and scholar.**
 
• He lived in the **Delhi Sultanate**, which was **ruled by Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firuz Shah** in modern-day Northern India.
 
• **He wrote:**
 
 
• **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi (also known as Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi),** a work on medieval India that spans the years between Ghiyasuddin Tughluq's reign and the first six years of Firoz Shah Tughluq's reign.
 
• **Fatwa-i-Jahandari,** which encouraged a hierarchy among Muslim communities in the Indian subcontinent, are his most iconic works.

questions.question: Dhananjaya Yashwant Chandrachud has been appointed as the ________ Chief Justice of India in October 2022.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50th.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Justice Dhananjaya Yashwant Chandrachud:**

 
 
• Justice DY Chandrachud is the **50th** and current Chief Justice of India having assumed office on 9th November 2022.
 
• In **May 2016**, he was named a **judge of the Indian Supreme Court**.
 
• In the past, he was a judge on the Bombay High Court from 2000 to 2013 and the **chief justice of the Allahabad High Court from 2013 to 2016.**
 
• In addition, he has served as the National Legal Services Authority's executive chairman (ex officio) in the past.
 
• The sole child of the **longest-serving chief justice in India, Y. V. Chandrachud.**
 
• He has served on benches that have handed down historic rulings on issues including the decriminalization of homosexuality, the Ram Janmabhoomi verdict, privacy verdicts, same-sex marriage cases, Sabarimala case, and the revocation of Jammu and Kashmir's special status.
 
 
 
• Chief Justice of India (CJI):
 
 
• The CJI and the Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President under clause (2) of Article 124 of the Constitution.
 
• Qualifications for being the CJI:
 
 
• He/She should 
 
 
• be a citizen of India.
 
• have been for at least five years a Judge of a High Court or of two or more such Courts in succession or
 
• have been for at least ten years an advocate of a High Court or of two or more such Courts in succession, or
 
• be, in the opinion of the President, a distinguished jurist.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Justice **Sabyasachi Mukharji** was the **20**th Chief Justice of India (CJI) having served from December 1989 to September 1990.
 
• Justice **Sam Piroj Bharucha** was the **30**th Chief Justice of India (CJI) having served from November 2001 to May 2002.
 
• Justice **Palanisamy Sathasivam** was the 40th Chief Justice of India (CJI) having served from July 2013 to 26 April 2014.
 
• Justice Uday Umesh Lalit was the 49th Chief Justice of India (CJI) having served from August 2022 to November 2022.
 
• Justice Nuthalapati Venkata Ramana was the 48th Chief Justice of India, having served from April 2021 to August 2022. 
 
• Justice Sharad Arvind Bobde was the 47th Chief Justice of India, having served from November 2019 to April 2021.

questions.question: The festival of Ram Navami is celebrated in the Hindu month of ________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaitra.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chaitra (March-April):** 

 
 
• In the Hindu calendar, the** first month is Chaitra** and is highly fortunate.
 
• Occurs in **March or April on the Gregorian calendar**.
 
• The Hindu New Year, known in **Maharashtra as Gudi Padwa**, in **Andhra Pradesh and Telangana as Ugadi**, and in **other parts of India as Chaitra Navratri**, ushers in the month.
 
• The month is** linked to fresh starts, development, and wealth** as well as the **start of the spring season.**
 
 
 
• **Ram Navami:**
 
 
• Ram Navami is a Hindu festival that** celebrates the birth of Lord Rama**, one of the **most revered deities in Hinduism.**
 
• It** falls on the ninth day of Shukla Paksha in the Hindu month of Chaitra**, which usually falls in March or April according to the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The festival is celebrated with great enthusiasm and devotion by Hindus all over the world, with special prayers, fasting, and offerings being made to Lord Rama and his consort Sita.
 
• The celebrations include processions, singing of devotional songs, and recitation of the Ramayana, the epic story of Lord Rama's life and deeds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashwin (September-October):** 

 
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, **Ashwin, the seventh month**, is connected to the** celebration of Navratri,** a holiday **honoring the divine feminine force.**
 
• Additionally, the month is linked to the** celebration of Dussehra, a festival honoring Lord Rama's victory over the demon king Ravana. **
 
 
 
• **Kartik (October-November):**
 
 
• The Hindu calendar's** eighth month, Kartik**, is linked to the **celebration of Diwali, the festival of lights.**
 
• The month is also linked to the **observance of Karva Chauth,** a festival **honoring the marriage union of husband and wife.**
 
• It is also **linked with festival of Bhai Dooj.**
 
 
 
• **Phalguna (February-March):**
 
 
• The** Hindu calendar's twelfth and final month, Phalguna**, occurs in** February or March on the Gregorian calendar.**
 
• It is the **month of Holi**, the widely renowned **festival of colors** that ushers in **India's springtime.**
 
• People of all ages celebrate the holiday with great excitement, playing with colors, indulging in traditional sweets and delicacies, and praying to Lord Krishna.
 
• In addition to Holi, Phalguna is the site of several significant celebrations,** including Shivratri and Holika Dahan.**

questions.question: Battle of Plassey was fought in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1757.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Battle of Plassey:**

 
 
• The Plassey battle took place **in 1757** at **West Bengal's Plassey, east of the Bhagirathi River.**
 
• The last independent **Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah** faced up against **Robert Clive's British East India Company** troops.
 
• Following the death of his grandfather Alavardi Khan, Siraj-ud-Daulah, the then-Nawab of Bengal, took over.
 
• Siraj was already wary of the East India Company's increasing influence because to the British victory in the Carnatic.
 
• In **June 1756,** the enraged Nawab marched to Calcutta and **took control of Fort William. **
 
• Siraj imprisoned 146 British detainees in a tiny lair in Calcutta; 123 of them perished from suffocation. It is notoriously referred to as the Calcutta **"Black Hole."**
 
• After the Nawab of Bengal tragically defeated the British, Robert Clive's formidable force was dispatched from Madras to depose the nawab and fortify British rule in Bengal.
 
• Nawab's defeat was **aided by Mir Jafar,** who led around one-third of the Bengali army, choosing not to participate in the conflict.
 
• The Nawab attempted to flee with his army under duress, but** Miran, Mir Jafar's son, assassinated him.**
 
• **Clive crowned Mir Jafar as the Nawab of Bengal **and placed him on the throne of Murshidabad following the Battle of Plassey.
 
• In accordance with the deal, **Mir Jafar offered the firm the Zamindari of 24 Parganas, a group of villages in Bengal,** in order to appease the British.
 
• But this was insufficient to appease the British, and as a result, he lost his position as Nawab of Bengal and was replaced by his son-in-law Mir Kasim.
 
 
 
• **The Battle is regarding a historic turning point for British in India; it established political and military supremacy of the British in Bengal.**

questions.question: Which among the following articles of the Indian Constitution relates to the Attorney General of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 76.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Attorney General of India:**

 
 
• **Article 76** of the Indian Constitution deals with the **appointment, duties, and qualifications of the Attorney General of India.**

 
 
• The Attorney General of India will be **appointed by the President **from among those who meet the **requirements to be appointed as Supreme Court judges.**
 
• The Attorney General will **serve as long as the President so desires.**
 
 
 
• He is the **chief law officer** in the country.
 
 
• He provides l**egal advice to the Government of India** and represents the Government in legal matters.
 
• He also has the** power to appear in any court of law in India** and can **take part in any proceedings** that affect the Government of India.
 
• Thus he have the **right of audience in all Indian courts while carrying out his duties.**
 
 
 
• Under **Article 88 **of the Indian Constitution, he is **free to participate in and speak at any session of the Houses of Parliament**, as well as in** any joint session**, and to be **appointed to any committee of the Parliament**; however, **he is not entitled to vote. **
 
• He is entitled to all the **privileges and immunities that are granted to members of Parliament.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• GST Council:

 
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a replacement for the Value-Added Tax (VAT) in India and is levied on the supply of goods and services.
 
• The tax came into effect from 1 July 2017 through the implementation of the 101st Amendment of the Constitution of India by the Indian government.
 
• It inserted Article 279-A in the Constitution of India which empowered the President to constitute a GST Council by an order.
 
• President issued the order in 2016 and constituted the Council.
 
• Composition of the Goods and Services Tax Council:
 
 
• The Union Finance Minister as the Chairperson.
 
• The Union Minister of State in-charge of Revenue or Finance.
 
• The Minister in-charge of Finance or Taxation or any other Minister nominated by each state government.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Metropolitan Planning Committee:**
 
 
• **Article 243 ZE** says that there shall be constituted in every Metropolitan area a **Metropolitan Planning Committee **to prepare a draft development plan for the Metropolitan area as a whole.
 
• A** state's legislature** shall provide **by law** for the makeup of these committees and the procedure for filling their seats.
 
 
 
• **State Finance Commission:**
 
 
• The** 73rd Constitutional Amendments Act, 1992 **established the **State Finance Commission (SFC)** as an entity to organize and simplify fiscal interactions between the States and sub-States in India.
 
• Every five years, the **State Governor** is required by **Article 243I **of the **Constitution to form a Finance Commission.**
 
• The Finance Commission established under Article 243 I of the Constitution is **mandated by Article 243Y to examine the financial standing of the Municipalities and provide recommendations to the Governor.**

questions.question: Husk of a coconut is made of ________ tissue.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclerenchyma.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The husk of a coconut is made up of sclerenchyma tissue.**
 
• **Permanent** and **Meristematic** tissues are **two types of plant tissue**.
 
• **Permanent tissues:**
 
 
• Although these cells can **no longer spread**, they are **specialized to provide the plant with strength, elasticity, and flexibility.**
 
• These tissues also fall into the following categories:
 
 
• **Simple Permanent Tissue**
 
• **Complex Permanent Tissue**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma:**
 
 
• It is type of **Simple Permanent Tissue.**
 
• These are** lengthy, dead cells** whose **cell walls have lignin deposits** in them. 
 
• There are **no spaces between the cells**. 
 
• Sclerenchyma surrounds the vascular tissues in stems and leaves, as well as the **coating of seeds and nuts.**
 
• The plant gets its strength from its sclerenchyma.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Permanent Tissue: **

 
 
• Depending on what they are used for, they can be divided into parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma.

 
 
• **Parenchyma:**

 
 
• These are multigonal,** living cells** with intercellular gaps between them and a large central vacuole. 
 
• Pith and ground tissue are produced by parenchymatous cells.
 
• Chlorenchyma is the term used to describe parenchyma that contains chloroplasts. **Photosynthesis is aided by the chlorenchyma.**
 
• Aerenchyma is the term for parenchyma that has large air gaps in it. The primary **function of the aerenchyma is buoyancy.**
 
• Certain parenchymatous cells serve as starch storage compartments in fruits and vegetables.
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• These are** live**, elongated cells with minuscule spaces between them.
 
• Pectin and cellulose make up their cell walls.
 
• It **provides plants with mechanical support and a flexible structural framework.**
 
• It is found on the margins of leaves and stems.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Complex Permanent Tissue: **Phloem and xylem are examples of these tissues. 
 
 
• **Xylem:**
 
 
• It **facilitates the movement of water and dissolved materials throughout the plant.**
 
• The various parts of the xylem consist of parenchyma, vessels, tracheids, and xylem fibers.
 
• Lignin makes up the xylem fibers and cheids, which give the plant structural support.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• **Food particles can be transported with the help of phloem.**
 
• Complementary cells, sieve cells, sieve tubes, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma make up phloem.

questions.question: _________ is a trade policy that doesn‘t restrict imports or exports.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Free trade.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Free Trade:**

__
 
• It is a **trade policy that** promotes the **exchange of goods and services between countries without any restrictions**, such as tariffs, quotas, or other trade barriers.
 
• The **India-UAE CEPA **is the most recent of India's twelve free trade agreements.
 
• In 2020, India made the decision to withdraw from the Asia-Pacific region's massive Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership.
 
• India has reaped only meager gains from the Free Trade Agreement with South Korea.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Fair Trade:**

 
• It is a trade policy that aims to promote greater equity in international trade, particularly **for small-scale producers and workers in developing countries**.
 
• It focuses on **improving working conditions**, promoting **sustainable production practices**, and ensuring **fair prices for producers.**

**Local Trade:**

 
• It refers to the **exchange of goods and services within a local community or region**, often with a focus on supporting small businesses, reducing transportation costs and environmental impact, and promoting local culture and identity.

**Swiss Trade:**

 
• It may refer to the **trade policies and practices of Switzerland**, which is known for its **openness to international trade**, particularly in the areas of finance, manufacturing, and services.
 
• **Switzerland** is also a member of the **World Trade Organization (WTO) **and has signed numerous free trade agreements with other countries and regions.

questions.question: Who was the first transgender to be honoured with Padma Shri?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narthaki Natraj.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

**Narthaki Natraj:**

 
• She was **born in** the Tamil Nadu **village of Anuppanadi**, which is close to Madurai.
 
• She is the **first transgender person to be honoured with the Padma Shri Award.**
 
• She is also honoured with the **SNA Puraskar **and Tamil Nadu's state award, **"Kalaimamani”.**

**Padma Shri:**

 
• The Padma Shri, which is also written **Padma Shree, is the fourth-highest civilian honor** granted by the Indian Republic, ranking behind the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan, and Padma Bhushan.
 
• Awardees are chosen for their "distinguished contribution in various spheres of **activity including the arts, education, industry, literature, science, acting, medicine, social service and public affairs."**
 
• The award was **established on January 2, 1954.**
 
• **Every year on India's Republic Day,** the Indian government bestows this honour.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

**​****Karthik Chandra Rath:**

 
• He has directed more than 500 plays and written more than 100 plays.
 
• He brought ground-breaking ideas to Odia play in the areas of stagecraft, scriptwriting, and direction.
 
• He established the **Utkal Yuva Sanskrutika Sangh in Cuttack**, which participated in national theater festivals.
 
• **Kendriya Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**,** Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**, and **Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award** were among the distinguished honors he received.

**Shanti Devi:**

 
• President Ram Nath Kovind presented her with the esteemed Padma Shri award on November 9, 2021.
 
• She made a significant **contribution to **the state's **Maoist-affected** districts being peaceful again.

A glossary of cricket terms:

 
 

 Terms
 Explanation
 
 

 Leg-Before Wicket (LBW)
 It's a way to get the batter out. In other words, the hitter is out if the umpire determines that the ball struck any portion of the batter's body—typically the leg—prior to striking the bat or missing the bat and would have struck the stumps.
 
 

 Maiden
 An over where no runs that are attributable to the bowler are scored (byes or leg-byes may be scored in this over, though, as these don't count against the bowler).
 
 

 Wide Ball
 A delivery that pitches too far away from the batsman and so proves impossible to score off. The umpire will single this by stretching his arms out horizontally; an extra will be added to the total and the ball will be bowled again.
 
 

 Bouncer
 A short-pitched ball which passes the batsman at chest or head height
 
 

 Chinaman
 A ball bowled by a left-arm slow bowler that turns into the right-hand batsman, in effect a left-arm legspinner. Named after Puss Achong.
 
 

 Mankad
 A term popular mainly in indoor cricket - but also fairly popular in Australia for outdoor cricket. Mankad is when the bowler brings his arm around and, instead of releasing the ball, runs out the non-striker by whipping off the bails. This type of dismissal is rare - and usually a warning is given to the batsman beforehand. Named after Vinod Mankad, who twice dismissed Australian Bill Brown this way.
 
 

 Doosra
 A Hindi/Urdu word which means "second" or "other", the doosra is the offspinner's version of the googly, delivered out of the back of the hand and turning away from the right-hand batsman.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure the vibrations during an earthquake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seismograph.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Seismograph:**

__
 
• It is equipment that monitors and records the motion of the ground caused by earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and other seismic phenomena.
 
• **Seismic vibrations cause the drum to revolve and the weighted pen to move** back and forth **when an earthquake occurs **in the ground.
 
• It is made up of a seismometer—a sensor that senses ground motion—and a recorder, which captures the seismometer's data.
 
• The three-dimensional **earthquake source and magnitude are measured by a network of seismometers.**
 
• With seismographs, one may determine:
 
 
• The earthquake's location.
 
• The earthquake's depth.
 
• The earthquake's magnitude.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Mercalli scale:**

 
• It is used **to measure an earthquake's intensity.**
 
• **Observable data is the basis** of the Mercalli scale.
 
• The scale **describes **the intensity of the **earthquake at twelve levels**.

**Hygrometer:**

 
• It is a specialized **device that determines the relative humidity **in a closed or open space.
 
• The **first hygrometer was created in 1783 by** Swiss physicist and geologist **Horace Bénédict de Saussur.**
 
 
• He used human hair to measure humidity.
 
 
 
• It functions through a process called **evaporative cooling.**

**Richter Scale:**

 
• **Charles Richter** created it in the 1930s.
 
• It is a **numerical system** used to indicate the** strength **(or magnitude) **of earthquakes.**
 
• It gives the energy produced by an earthquake a magnitude number. 
 
• It is a base-10 logarithmic scale, where magnitude is expressed as the logarithm of the seismic wave amplitude divided by an arbitrary, minor amplitude.

questions.question: What was the slogan of the 2011 Census of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Our Census - Our Future.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Census of India 2011**

__
 
• It **started on April 1, 2010.**
 
• "**Our Census, Our Future"** was the **2011 census's slogan**.
 
• **India's population,** according to the **2011 Census,** is **estimated to be 1.21 billion.**
 
• This marked the commencement of the **15th Census of India** and the **7th Census of Independent India** (2011).
 
• The Indian **Census Commissioner** for 2011 was** C. Chandramouli.**
 
• The 2011 India Census was carried out in** two phases:**
 
 
• House listing and Housing Census (April to September 2010).
 
• Population Enumeration (9th to 28 February 2011).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 1948 Census Act governs how the census is carried out.
 
• The Indian Home Minister at the time, **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, spearheaded the bill for this Act.**
 
• The Indian Constitution's **Article 246** declares the population census to be a **Union subject**.
 
• It is mentioned in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution under serial number 69.
 
• The Ministry of Home Affairs' Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner oversees the decennial census.
 
• According to the 2011 census, the overall **literacy rate **in India is **74%.**
 
• The **population density **was** ****382 persons per square kilometer **in 2011.
 
• India's **sex ratio**, as per the 2011 census, **is 943.**
 
• India's **child sex ratio is 918**, the lowest since the country's independence, as per Census 2011.
